title: The FCRA Amendment Bill: tighter rules for foreign-funded NGOs
dek: A bill that would let the government take over assets of NGOs that lose their foreign-funding licence is now with a parliamentary committee.
seoTitle: FCRA Amendment Bill 2026 timeline: what it proposes and where it stands
bigLabel: Members of the joint committee examining the bill

glance.what: The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 is being examined by a 31-member joint parliamentary committee. It is not yet law.
glance.why: It would affect thousands of NGOs, charities and religious bodies that receive foreign funding, including what happens to their assets if they lose registration.
glance.next: The committee’s report is due by the end of the first week of the 2026 Winter Session.

forYou: If you run or work with an FCRA-registered organisation, the current Act and the 2026 Rules still apply. The bill changes nothing until Parliament passes it.

upcoming.label: Winter Session

events.title: Bill introduced in the Lok Sabha
events.summary: It proposes a designated authority to take control of assets of NGOs whose FCRA licences are cancelled, surrendered or lapsed.

events.title: Separate FCRA Rules, 2026 come into force
events.summary: Revised rules are notified and take effect. They are distinct from the amendment bill, which is still pending.

events.title: Sent to a joint committee amid protests
events.summary: After opposition parties and minority groups demand its withdrawal, the Lok Sabha refers the bill to a 31-member joint parliamentary committee.

events.title: Committee formed, chaired by Sanjay Jaiswal
events.summary: The joint committee is constituted with BJP MP Sanjay Jaiswal as chair.

events.title: Home Ministry briefs the committee
events.summary: The panel begins detailed examination after a briefing from the Ministry of Home Affairs.
